analysis:
All changed files are test-only (ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Distributed/ClusterApproval/*); no production code, endpoint, key handling or attestation path is modified in the supplied units, so no regressions to canonical assets or trust boundaries are introduced here.

Examined: (1) ClusterApprovalFixture.swift adds a Shape enum (pipeline / qwen27TensorParallel with optional tensor assistant). Fixture files are created 0700/0600 under a private root and removed in deinit. Link secrets are the constant 32 bytes of 0x07, which is test-only. (2) ClusterApprovalServiceStartTests.swift adds a supervised/unsupervised environment injection and tests asserting that a coordinator-paired member part beats into its own heartbeat file (partHealthPath), never the service's healthPath. The tests also assert that an empty heartbeat name stays empty. This documents a liveness/availability fix; the production implementation (ClusterService.partEnvironment, ClusterServiceAgent.partHealthPath) is not in the supplied units, so it is unverified here. (3) ClusterApprovalTensorAssistantTests.swift (new) asserts that a setup with the unqualified tensor assistant is refused by the leader before any part stops or anything is sent to the peer, and is refused by the follower with a plain reason, leaving its setup bytes unchanged. The tests encode a fail-closed expectation. (4) ClusterApprovalWatchTests.swift encodes that coordinator-side negotiation failures do not count as quick ends, so they cannot trigger a failing fallback. The tests encode that a failing set-aside expires after an hour (setAt), that a legacy record without setAt is past the hour, and that a future setAt is treated as expired. Together these bound how long an approval stays set aside, which affects availability and approval retry and not the confidentiality or authorization guarantees.

Open integration questions: the production implementations behind these tests (ClusterApprovalCheck.setAside/step, ClusterApprovalFallback.failingSeconds, the tensorAssistant refusal in ClusterApprovalSync, and ClusterService.partEnvironment) are not in the supplied units. Their security behavior is not verified by this pass, only the test expectations. No threat-model IDs appear materially affected.
